vulnerability_type: Vulnerable third party component on the IPC deserialization boundary
summary: Cargo.lock resolves rkyv to 0.8.15, which is inside the affected range of a published use-after-free and two out-of-bounds reads in archive validation, and every Xous inter-process message the vault accepts is deserialized with it.
explanation: Cargo.toml requests rkyv "0.8.8" as a caret requirement and the lockfile resolves 0.8.15. RUSTSEC-2026-0233 (use-after-free during deserialization), RUSTSEC-2026-0234 and RUSTSEC-2026-0235 (out-of-bounds reads from insufficient archive validation) are all fixed only in 0.8.17, and GHSA-vfvv-c25p-m7mm is fixed in 0.8.16. Nine call sites consume archives from peer memory messages via Buffer::to_original and each ends in unwrap or expect. main.rs:104 registers the vault server with None as the maximum connection count, so the Xous name server does not bound which processes may connect.
malicious_actor: a process on the badge able to connect to the vault server and send it a memory message
parameter: rkyv archive bytes in a Xous shared memory page, consumed by Buffer::to_original()
trigger_flow: attacker process -> xous::connect to SERVER_NAME_VAULT2 -> memory message -> Buffer::from_memory_message -> to_original::<T, _>() -> rkyv archive validation
malicious_input_example: a crafted rkyv archive exercising RUSTSEC-2026-0233 sent as the body of a VaultOp::HandleQr memory message
